newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 25.

text.p: U.S. electric utility Duke Power Co has agreed to buy natural gas pipeline PanEnergy Corp for about $50 a share in stock or $7.7 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported.
- Wireless company NextWave Telecom Inc has agreed to purchase $200 million in equipment during the next two years from Lucent Technologies Inc.
- U.S. oil company Chevron Corp plans to end all offshore crude oil production in California between 1999 and 2001, years sooner than it had originally planned.
- ABN AMRO agreed to buy Standard Federal Bank for $1.9 billion.
- Europe will bring Italy's lira back into its exchange-rate mechanism.
- An accounting group is considering making it harder for software companies to post revenue immediately from contracts.
- Continental Grain and an overseas affiliate agreed to pay the federal government a total of $35 million to settle a fraud case.
- Norteastern Utilities is not likely to reopen any of its troubled Millstone nuclear reactors until the second half of 1997.
- Canada's nuclear power agency is to sign a pact to build a $3 billion nuclear power plant in China.
- The Dow Jones industrial average rose 53.29 to a record 6,471.76.
- Lloyd's of London plans to offer up to $1 million for the legal bills of companies that sue competitors for patent infringement.
- Symantec Corp's chief executive officer was cleared of 1992 charges that he stole trade secrets.
- Mark Whitacre filed a wrongful dismissal suit against Archer Daniels Midland Co.
- America Online Inc reached an agreement with Washington state to improve consumer options for its new pricing plan.
- More than ever before, bonds are being traded all the time around the world.
- Genetics Institute Inc is waiting for a decision from American Home Products Corp on whether it will buy it out.
